$comment: Registry of third-party web assets vendored into the app.
The artifact/diagram/math renderers are WebViews. Everything they execute ships
inside the APK and the iOS bundle -- nothing is fetched at runtime. That is a hard
requirement, not a preference: F-Droid rejects apps that download executable code
without explicit opt-in consent, and a CDN <script src> is exactly that.
It also removes a failure mode that produced no error anywhere. While these were
hot-linked, an unversioned CDN URL silently served whatever the CDN resolved that
day: marked's `highlight` option was deleted upstream in v5 and the callback simply
stopped being called, and @babel/standalone drifted onto a new major. Neither broke
a build or a test -- they broke on user devices. Pinned files in git turn that class
of breakage into a reviewable diff.
Every entry is a version PIN. Bumping one is a deliberate act with a device test,
not a background upgrade -- see .claude/skills/update-web-assets.
Read and written by scripts/vendor-web-assets.py:
scripts/vendor-web-assets.py --check      verify the tree matches the lock (CI)
scripts/vendor-web-assets.py --sync       re-download every pin
scripts/vendor-web-assets.py --outdated   ask npm what newer versions exist
scripts/vendor-web-assets.py --bump ID V  repin one asset and re-download it
source.type:
npm  -- extracted from the package's official registry tarball. Preferred: the
bytes are the publisher's own, and --outdated can see past them.
url  -- a pinned URL, for the one build with no npm equivalent (see tailwind).
bundle -- npm packages a React artifact may `import`, bundled by esbuild into one
classic script each (scripts/artifact-modules: exact pins in package.json,
the transitive tree in package-lock.json, the bundling in build.mjs). These
bytes are NOT the publisher's own -- they are built here from the publishers'
sources, which is why the lock also hashes the recipe. Classic scripts, not
ES modules, because module scripts cannot load over file:// in Android
WebView (build.mjs explains). `modules` lists the specifiers each bundle
registers; the runner reads them from the generated VendoredWebAssets.MODULES.
The set mirrors web's Sandpack dependencies (standardDependencies in
upstream client/src/utils/artifacts.ts), watched in scripts/mirrors.json.
`sandbox_risk` records why a package that would fail the dependency policy
(unmaintained, or carrying an advisory) is acceptable inside the artifact WebView.
The argument is the same each time: an artifact is model-written JavaScript that
already runs with every privilege the page has, and a bundled library runs with
exactly those, so a flaw in one cannot grant what the artifact code could not do
itself. The page's walls are what matter: CSP default-src 'none' (no fetch/XHR),
form-action 'none', remote main-frame navigation refused on both platforms
(isRemoteMainFrameNavigation, LocalOnlyNavigationPolicy), no file access, and no JS
bridge on React pages (the inline hosts bind MermaidBridge for mermaid only and the
height reporter for office previews only). NOT a wall: img-src https: stays open, so
any artifact, and any library in it, can send data out in an image URL. Re-read this
list before relying on the argument: if a wall moves, every sandbox_risk below needs
a fresh look.
A file entry may carry its own `url` to pull one file from outside the tarball,
for packages that ship no LICENSE on npm (mermaid).
LICENSE files are vendored alongside the code, not optional: MIT and BSD-3 both
require the notice to travel with the distribution, and hot-linking was the only
reason we were not already distributing it.

assets.why: Renders LaTeX in ordinary chat messages. Highest-traffic asset here: it loads whenever a message contains math, with no user action.
assets.pin_reason: Version the renderers were written against. KaTeX is API-stable across patches; bump freely after a device check.

assets.why: Renders ```mermaid blocks in chat messages and mermaid artifacts.
assets.pin_reason: MUST stay on the v10 line. v11+ ships ESM-only, which fails in Android WebView under loadDataWithBaseURL with "Unexpected token '{'". --outdated will report v11 as available; do not take it without first proving an ESM entry point loads in the oldest supported WebView.

files.note: mermaid's npm tarball ships no LICENSE file; taken from the matching git tag.

assets.pin_reason: Vendors lib/marked.umd.js, the published UMD build, which exists in both v15 and v18 and is the stable path forward. The old CDN URL pointed at a root marked.min.js that recent releases stopped shipping -- jsDelivr was silently serving v15 while npm latest was v18.

assets.why: The supported way to feed highlight.js into marked. marked deleted its built-in `highlight` option in v5; without this extension the callback is silently never invoked.
assets.pin_reason: Tracks marked's major. Re-check compatibility whenever marked is bumped.

Deliberately @highlightjs/cdn-assets, NOT the `highlight.js` package. The main package ships CommonJS only -- its lib/*.js end in `module.exports` and call `require()`, so in a WebView <script> they throw and never define `hljs`. cdn-assets is the team's browser build. Only the two themes the renderer selects are vendored; the package carries 258.

assets.why: In-browser JIT compiler so HTML and React artifacts can use Tailwind utility classes.
assets.pin_reason: The only asset here with no npm equivalent: Tailwind v3 never published a browser build, so this is the Play CDN artifact from Tailwind Labs' own host, pinned to an immutable version path. Source for it is tailwindlabs/tailwindcss v3.4.17 (MIT). @tailwindcss/browser on npm is v4 only, and v4 renamed or dropped utilities that model-generated artifacts still emit (bg-opacity-*, flex-shrink-*, the default border color), so moving to it is a behaviour change to make deliberately, not a provenance cleanup to do quietly.

assets.why: Compiles a React artifact's JSX in the WebView before it is imported as a module.
assets.pin_reason: Pinned to the 7.x line the runner was written against. The old URL carried no version at all and had already drifted onto Babel 8, which nothing here was tested against.

assets.why: The React runtime a React artifact renders against.
assets.pin_reason: React 18. The UMD production build is vendored because npm ships no browser-ready ESM for React 18 -- that gap is the entire reason the old code reached for esm.sh. The runner bridges UMD globals back into the import map, so artifacts still `import React from 'react'` unchanged. React 19 dropped UMD builds entirely; moving to it means solving module delivery first.
Must match the react pin exactly. Two copies of React in one page break hooks with "invalid hook call".

assets.why: Unzips a DOCX for docx-preview, which reads the global JSZip. The server's DOCX preview document (packages/api/src/files/documents/html.ts, DOCX_PREVIEW_CDN) loads it from jsDelivr; the client rewrites that tag to this copy. Dual-licensed MIT OR GPL-3.0-or-later; distributed under MIT. The minified build bundles pako (MIT), noticed in its header.
assets.pin_reason: Exact match to the server's DOCX_PREVIEW_CDN pin, which is what the client rewrites. The rewrite is version-exact, so a server on any other version gets its tag stripped and shows its mammoth fallback rather than running code it was not written against. Bump only in lockstep with upstream's DOCX_PREVIEW_CDN (watched in scripts/mirrors.json as office-preview-docx-cdn). These bytes equal the server's SRI pin: sha384-+mbV2IY1Zk/X1p/nWllGySJSUN8uMs+gUAN10Or95UBH0fpj6GfKgPmgC5EXieXG.

assets.why: Renders a DOCX office preview at page fidelity. The server's DOCX preview document loads it from jsDelivr (DOCX_PREVIEW_CDN); the client rewrites that tag to this copy. Without it the document shows its server-rendered mammoth fallback.
assets.pin_reason: Exact match to the server's DOCX_PREVIEW_CDN pin, for the same reason as jszip: the rewrite is version-exact and a mismatch falls back rather than runs. Bump with jszip, in lockstep with upstream. These bytes equal the server's SRI pin: sha384-Fw+ZM2MtvxCe867uRzZY5GtGP+gs0NLvrlJS768RZWuKhOHMN4Fln3i3gMt1NSyQ. The server's PPTX renderer, pptx-preview, is deliberately NOT vendored: its package.json says ISC, but the tarball ships no LICENSE and its README restricts the source to personal study and forbids republishing or modifying it, so it is not FOSS. PPTX previews show the server's slide-list fallback instead.

assets.why: Icons for React artifacts. The server's artifact prompt tells the model lucide-react is importable, so it is the most common third-party import an artifact makes.
assets.pin_reason: The server's prompt names lucide-react@0.394.0 exactly (packages/api/src/prompts/artifacts/index.ts) and web resolves ^0.394.0, which caret keeps on 0.394.x. Later releases rename and remove icons, so an icon a model writes from the prompt would stop existing. Move only when upstream's prompt does (watched: artifact-prompt-libraries, artifact-sandpack-dependencies).

assets.why: Charts for React artifacts. Advertised by the server's artifact prompt.
assets.pin_reason: AHEAD of web on purpose: web pins 2.12.7, but npm marks the whole 2.x line deprecated, and the server's prompt names no version -- its only example is `import { LineChart, XAxis, ... } from "recharts"`, which v3 keeps. v3 dropped some v2 internals (the activeIndex props, CategoricalChartState, Customized's injected props), so an artifact leaning on those renders on web and not here. Needs react-is on the React 18 line (pinned 18.3.1 in package.json): react-is 19 does not recognise React 18 elements, and recharts would see every child as foreign.

assets.why: 3D scenes for React artifacts. Advertised by the server's artifact prompt.
assets.pin_reason: Web's ^0.167.1, which resolves to 0.167.1. Only the `three` entry point is bundled: the addons (`three/addons/...`, `three/examples/jsm/...`, e.g. OrbitControls) are not, and an artifact importing one gets the not-bundled error naming it. The prompt promises only `three`; the addons would add several MB.

assets.why: Date formatting for React artifacts. Advertised by the server's artifact prompt.
assets.pin_reason: Latest release of web's ^3.3.1. v4 changed time-zone handling; stay on 3.x while web does. `date-fns/locale` is not bundled (English only), and the shadcn-ui bundle carries its own copy for react-day-picker.

assets.why: Routing inside a React artifact (MemoryRouter / HashRouter tabs). In web's Sandpack dependencies, not advertised by the prompt.
assets.pin_reason: AHEAD of web (^6.11.2) on purpose. Every 6.x is covered by two advisories fixed only in 7.x, and 7.x still publishes react-router-dom as a re-export of react-router, so imports written for 6 keep resolving.
assets.sandbox_risk: GHSA-wrjc-x8rr-h8h6 (open redirect via a backslash in <Link>/useNavigate) only lets a link navigate somewhere unexpected; an artifact can already set location.href, and the WebView refuses every remote main-frame navigation. GHSA-337j-9hxr-rhxg (constructor injection in deserializeErrors) is on the SSR hydration path, which a browser-only page never takes. Neither reaches anything here, so 7.x is taken because it is free, not because 6.x was dangerous in this sandbox.

assets.why: The parameter panel three.js demos use. In web's Sandpack dependencies, not advertised by the prompt.
assets.pin_reason: Web's ^0.7.9, and the last release there is.
assets.sandbox_risk: UNMAINTAINED: last release 2020, which the dependency policy would normally refuse. No advisories. It is a DOM widget that reads and writes properties on the objects the artifact hands it, so it can do nothing the artifact's own code could not. The user is still asked before an artifact loads it (`advisory`). The real cost is that nobody will fix it if a WebView change breaks it; if that happens, drop it from the registry rather than patching it.

licenses.title: shadcn/ui component sources, as embedded in LibreChat's packages/data-provider/src/artifacts.ts (MIT)

assets.why: The shadcn/ui components web mounts into every React artifact at /components/ui/*, which the server's prompt tells the model to import, plus the packages they are built on, which web also exposes directly. One bundle, so a component and an artifact importing the same Radix primitive share one copy (and one React context). The Drawer is the exception: it ships in the vaul bundle.
assets.pin_reason: Version is the upstream commit the component sources were taken from (UPSTREAM_VERSION's commit=); move it with a sync. The packages are the latest within web's carets, pinned exactly in scripts/artifact-modules/package.json. build.mjs refuses to build when upstream mounts a component this list omits (sharedFiles, plus the artifactUIComponents it spreads), or drops one it lists. tailwindcss-animate (in web's list) is a Tailwind plugin, not an importable module; web's Tailwind runs with no config, so it does nothing there either. The calendar component is written against react-day-picker 8's classNames keys and IconLeft/IconRight components, which 9.x renamed; web's caret resolves 9.x too, so both run the same code. Parity, not a bug to fix here.

licenses.title: shadcn/ui component sources, as embedded in LibreChat's packages/data-provider/src/artifacts.ts (MIT)

assets.why: The drawer primitive behind shadcn's Drawer, and that component. In web's Sandpack dependencies.
assets.pin_reason: Latest release of web's ^0.9.1. Its own bundle, apart from shadcn-ui, so declining it in the consent prompt keeps its code from running at all; that costs a second copy of @radix-ui/react-dialog and of the `cn` helper, which only load when a Drawer is imported. The Drawer source moves with the upstream commit in the shadcn-ui entry's version.
assets.sandbox_risk: ARCHIVED upstream (its README says it is unmaintained), last release Dec 2024, no advisories. A drawer widget running with the artifact's own privileges; see the $comment. The user is asked before an artifact loads it. If it breaks on a WebView update, drop this entry rather than patch it.
